title: Encapsulation and properties

youtube.title: Python Encapsulation and @property Explained | Python Programming EP 70
youtube.description: In this episode you will protect data behind a property, validate values in a setter and understand the underscore convention, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 Guard the data · 1:02 A read-only property · 1:44 The clerk at the counter · 2:18 Second program · 3:18 Recap · 3:48 Bug of the Day · 4:36 Challenge · 4:56 Next episode

scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: Encapsulation means keeping data safe inside the object, and letting outsiders in only through checks. In Python, a name with one leading underscore means, please do not touch directly. A property is the polite doorway. The at property decorator lets you read the value like a plain attribute, while a function runs behind the scenes. A setter, written with at name dot setter, can reject bad values. Think of a bank counter. You cannot reach into the vault. You ask the clerk, who checks first.

The clerk reads the value for you, or checks your new value before storing it. If your request is bad, the clerk refuses. That is encapsulation. The rules live in one place, next to the data.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: a property with no setter
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. Price is a read-only property, because it has no setter. Assigning item dot price equals sixty fails. Attribute error, property price of Item object has no setter. Add a setter with the same name, and assignment works. Or leave it out on purpose, to make the value read-only.

lines: AttributeError: property 'price' of 'Item' object has no setter

props.why: A property with only a getter is read-only. To allow assignment, add a setter with the same name.

scenes.onScreen: Why did the property get a setter? Because it was tired of being read-only.

challenge: Write an Item class whose price property rejects negative values with a ValueError.
challengeAnswer: Use @property price, and @price.setter with if value < 0: raise ValueError("price must not be negative").
